parse.title: Addiction suppression
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>
'''Addiction suppression''' is defined as the experience of a total or partial suppression of a psychological addiction to a specific substance and the cravings associated with it. This can occur as an effect which lasts long after the compound which induced it wears off or it can last only while the compound is still active. 

Addiction suppression is a rare effect that is most commonly associated with [[psychedelic]]s,<ref name="Nichols2016">{{cite journal|last1=Nichols|first1=D. E.|title=Psychedelics|journal=Pharmacological Reviews|volume=68|issue=2|year=2016|pages=264–355|issn=1521-0081|doi=10.1124/pr.115.011478}}</ref> [[psilocin]],<ref name="JohnsonGarcia-Romeu2014">{{cite journal|last1=Johnson|first1=Matthew W|last2=Garcia-Romeu|first2=Albert|last3=Cosimano|first3=Mary P|last4=Griffiths|first4=Roland R|title=Pilot study of the 5-HT2AR agonist psilocybin in the treatment of tobacco addiction|journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology|volume=28|issue=11|year=2014|pages=983–992|issn=0269-8811|doi=10.1177/0269881114548296}}</ref> [[LSD]],<ref name="KrebsJohansen2012">{{cite journal|last1=Krebs|first1=Teri S|last2=Johansen|first2=Pål-Ørjan|title=Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) for alcoholism: meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials|journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology|volume=26|issue=7|year=2012|pages=994–1002|issn=0269-8811|doi=10.1177/0269881112439253}}</ref> [[ibogaine]]<ref name="Brown2013">{{cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=Thomas|title=Ibogaine in the Treatment of Substance Dependence|journal=Current Drug Abuse Reviews|volume=6|issue=1|year=2013|pages=3–16|issn=18744737|doi=10.2174/15672050113109990001}}</ref> and [[N-acetylcysteine]] (NAC).<ref name="Moran2005">{{cite journal|last1=Moran|first1=M. M.|title=Cystine/Glutamate Exchange Regulates Metabotropic Glutamate Receptor Presynaptic Inhibition of Excitatory Transmission and Vulnerability to Cocaine Seeking|journal=Journal of Neuroscience|volume=25|issue=27|year=2005|pages=6389–6393|issn=0270-6474|doi=10.1523/JNEUROSCI.1007-05.2005}}</ref></onlyinclude>
===Analysis===
In terms of psychedelics, this effect seems to be primarily triggered by the psychological self-reflection that can manifest through a combination of effects. These primarily include [[analysis enhancement]], [[personal bias suppression]], and [[introspection]]. The intensity and effectiveness of this experience occurring under the influence of a psychedelic is unpredictable and depends on a variety of factors such as [[dosage]], [[setting]], [[Responsible drug use#State of mind|state of mind]], and a general willingness to change.

In comparison, [[N-acetylcysteine]] and a small number of other compounds seem to suppress feelings of addiction in a more direct and consistent manner. This is thought to occur as a result of their action on [[glutamate|glutaminergic]] and [[dopamine]]rgic pathways which may reverse brain functions that have become disturbed by heavy drug addiction.<ref name="Moran2005" /><ref name="PettorrusoDe Risio2014">{{cite journal|last1=Pettorruso|first1=Mauro|last2=De Risio|first2=Luisa|last3=Martinotti|first3=Giovanni|last4=Di Pathological Gambling: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives|journal=BioMed Research International|volume=2014|year=2014|pages=1–11|issn=2314-6133|doi=10.1155/2014/109786}}</ref><ref name="ReissnerKalivas2010">{{cite journal|last1=Reissner|first1=Kathryn J.|last2=Kalivas|first2=Peter W.|title=Using glutamate homeostasis as a target for treating addictive disorders|journal=Behavioural Pharmacology|volume=21|issue=5-6|year=2010|pages=514–522|issn=0955-8810|doi=10.1097/FBP.0b013e32833d41b2}}</ref> This mechanism has been shown to provide relief for those who struggle with [[compulsive redosing]], reward behaviors, and psychological cravings, and has been shown to positively reverse [[nicotine]] addiction,<ref name="KnackstedtLaRowe2009">{{cite journal|last1=Kalivas|first1=Peter W.|last2=LaLumiere|first2=Ryan T.|last3=Knackstedt|first3=Lori|last4=Shen|first4=Haowei|title=Glutamate transmission in typically only manifest themselves while the person is still under the influence of the drug and do not seem to last beyond that.
